when: Caller asks for their current account balance or amount owed.
examples: how much do I owe right now
can you tell me my account balance
I just want to know what my balance is
say: Sure, let me pull up your balance.

when: Caller asks about the general status or standing of their account.
examples: is my account in good standing
what's the status of my account
can you check if my account is active
is everything okay with my account
say: Let me take a look at your account.

when: Caller asks how much of a service, data, or minutes they have used.
examples: how much data have I used this month
how many minutes do I have left
am I close to my limit
say: Let me check your usage for you.

when: Caller asks about recent transactions, charges, or activity on the account.
examples: what were my last few transactions
can you read me my recent activity
what was that charge on Tuesday
show me what posted this week
say: One moment while I look through your recent activity.

when: Caller gives identifying details such as name, number, or account id so they can be found.
examples: my account number is four five two one
my phone number is five five five one two one two
the email on file is jsmith at example
say: Thanks, give me a second to find that.

when: Caller wants to change or confirm contact details like address, phone, or email on the account.
examples: I need to update my address
can you change my email on file
I got a new phone number
what phone number do you have for me
say: Okay, let me bring up your contact details.

when: Caller wants to make a payment now.
examples: I'd like to pay my bill
can I make a payment over the phone
I want to pay what I owe today
let's take care of my payment
say: Happy to help with that payment.

when: Caller disputes or does not recognize a charge.
examples: I was charged twice for the same thing
there's a charge on here that's wrong
I want to dispute a payment
say: I'm sorry about that, let me look into the charge.

when: Caller asks for money back or a refund.
examples: can I get my money back
you owe me a refund for last month
say: Let me see what we can do about that.

when: Caller asks when a bill is due or when a payment is expected.
examples: when does my payment come out
what's the due date on my invoice
say: Let me check that date for you.

when: Caller says a payment or card was declined or failed.
examples: I tried to pay and it errored out
say: Okay, let me see what happened with that payment.

when: Caller wants to add, change, or ask about the payment method on file.
examples: I need to update my credit card
can I switch to a different card
which card do you have on file
I want to set up autopay
say: Sure, let me pull up your payment details.

when: Caller asks for an invoice, receipt, or an explanation of a bill.
examples: I need a copy of my invoice
why is my bill higher this month
can you send me a receipt
say: Let me go over that bill with you.

when: Caller wants to cancel a service, plan, or subscription.
examples: I want to cancel my subscription
how do I close my account
say: I understand, let me look at your options.

when: Caller wants to upgrade, downgrade, or switch plans.
examples: I want to switch to a cheaper plan
I'd like to change my package
what if I move to the premium tier
say: Sure, let me see what's available for you.

when: Caller wants to change details of an existing order or booking.
examples: I need to change my order
can I add something to what I ordered
I put in the wrong size
say: Okay, let me pull that up and see what can change.

when: Caller wants to cancel a specific order or booking.
examples: I don't want that order anymore
can you cancel the thing I ordered yesterday
I need to cancel my reservation
say: Got it, let me check where that order stands.

when: Caller wants to pause, freeze, or temporarily stop something.
examples: I'm going away, hold my service
I need to put it on hold for a couple months
say: Let me see if we can do that for you.

when: Caller wants to return or exchange a product.
examples: can I exchange it for another one
this doesn't fit, what do I do
how do I send it back
say: Okay, let me look at the return options.

when: Caller is angry or very upset in general terms.
examples: I am so fed up with this
this is the worst service ever
I can't believe how bad this is
say: I'm really sorry, I hear you.

when: Caller says the same problem keeps happening or they have called many times.
examples: this is the third time I'm calling
I keep having the same problem
I've already explained this to five people
say: I'm sorry you've had to call again, let me help.

when: Caller complains about long waits or slow response.
examples: why does everything take so long
I was on hold for an hour
nobody ever gets back to me
say: I apologize for the wait, I'm on it now.

when: Caller is upset specifically about money, fees, or being overcharged.
examples: I'm sick of being charged for nothing
this bill is a rip off
say: I understand, that's frustrating. Let me check.

when: Caller threatens to leave, cancel, or escalate publicly.
examples: I'm going to take my business elsewhere
if this isn't fixed I'm canceling
I'm going to leave a terrible review
I want to speak to someone above you
say: I want to make this right, let me look closely.

when: Caller expresses disappointment in a calmer, sad tone.
examples: this isn't what I was promised
I've been a customer for years and this is how you treat me
say: I'm sorry to hear that, let me see what I can do.

when: Caller says they were given wrong or conflicting information.
examples: someone told me something completely different
your website says one thing and you say another
I was told this would be free
that's not what the last agent said
say: Thanks for telling me, let me sort that out.

when: Caller directly asks to speak to a real person or live agent.
examples: can I talk to a real person
say: Understood, let me see about getting someone for you.

when: Caller asks for a supervisor or manager.
examples: let me speak to your supervisor
I want to talk to a manager
put your manager on the line
say: I'll see what I can do about that.

when: Caller asks whether they are speaking to a machine.
examples: am I talking to a robot
say: Good question, let me answer that for you.

when: Caller asks to be transferred to a particular department.
examples: can you transfer me to billing
I need the technical support team
connect me with the claims department
say: Okay, let me see about that transfer.

when: Caller asks for a specific named person.
examples: I need to talk to Mr. Patel
can I speak with the person I talked to yesterday
I want to reach Dave in accounting
say: Let me check whether they're available.

when: Caller asks for someone to call them back.
examples: have an agent give me a ring later
can you schedule a call back for me
say: Sure, let me look at callback options.

when: Caller says the automated assistant is not helping and wants another route.
examples: I need someone who can actually help
stop, just connect me to somebody
say: I'm sorry I'm not helping, let me try another way.

when: Caller opens with a plain greeting.
say: Hi there, thanks for calling.

when: Caller asks how the assistant is doing, as pleasantry.
say: Doing well, thanks for asking.

when: Caller greets and immediately begins stating a problem.
examples: hi, I'm calling because something's wrong with my order
hey, quick question about my account
hello, I need some help with a thing
good afternoon, I have a problem
say: Hi, glad you called. I'm listening.

when: Caller asks who they have reached or who is speaking.
say: You've reached the support line, happy to help.

when: Caller makes casual small talk unrelated to the task.
say: I hear you, it's been one of those days.

when: Caller checks whether the line is live or anyone is listening.
say: Yes, I'm here and I can hear you.

when: Caller says they need help without saying with what.
examples: can you help me with something
say: Of course, I'd be glad to help.

when: Caller thanks the assistant after help.
say: You're very welcome.

when: Caller says goodbye or ends the call.
examples: that's all, have a good one
say: Take care, and thanks for calling.

when: Caller says they need nothing more.
say: Great, glad we could help today.

when: Caller says they have one more question.
examples: before you go, can I ask something
say: Of course, go ahead.

when: Caller wishes the assistant well or expresses warmth.
say: Thank you, that's kind. You too.

when: Caller thanks the assistant but is waiting for more action or a final answer.
examples: okay thanks, so what happens now
great, thank you, and then what
got it, thanks, anything else I should do
say: You bet, let me confirm the next step.

when: Caller asks the assistant to repeat the last thing said.
say: Sure, let me say that again.

when: Caller says the assistant is too fast or needs it slower.
examples: I couldn't catch that, slowly please
say: Of course, I'll take it slower.

when: Caller asks what a term or statement meant.
examples: what do you mean by that
I don't understand what that means
say: Good question, let me explain that more simply.

when: Caller asks for a simpler or different explanation.
examples: can you put that another way
explain it like I'm new to this
say: Sure, let me try that a different way.

when: Caller spells out or corrects a name, number, or word.
examples: it's spelled J O N E S
no, it's with a K not a C
let me spell that for you
the last name is Nguyen, N G U Y E N
say: Thanks, let me make sure I have that right.

when: Caller corrects something the assistant said or got wrong.
examples: no, that's not what I said
say: Sorry about that, let me correct it.

when: Caller asks which option or item the assistant is referring to.
examples: which one are you talking about
say: Let me clarify which one I mean.

when: Caller cannot sign in or access their account online.
examples: it won't let me into my account
the login page keeps giving me an error
say: Sorry about the trouble, let me help you get in.

when: Caller says service, internet, or an app is not working or is down.
say: Let me check if there's an issue on our end.

when: Caller reports trouble with a specific device or product.
examples: the thing is making a weird noise
say: Okay, let me help troubleshoot that with you.

when: Caller reads or describes a specific error message.
examples: it says error code five zero three
there's a message that says something went wrong
say: Thanks for that detail, let me look it up.

when: Caller reports slowness, lag, or poor quality.
say: Let me look at what's going on with that.

when: Caller asks how to do something in the product or app.
examples: how do I reset my router
where do I find the settings
how do I turn that feature on
I can't figure out how to set this up
say: Sure, I'll walk you through it.

when: Caller says they have already tried the usual fixes.
examples: I've tried turning it off and on
I did all the troubleshooting steps
I've already reset my password twice
say: Understood, I'll skip the basics and dig deeper.

when: Caller asks where their order or package is.
examples: I haven't gotten my package yet
what's the status of my shipment
say: Let me track that order for you.

when: Caller asks when an order will arrive.
examples: how long until I get it
say: Let me check the delivery estimate.

when: Caller says an order is late or overdue.
examples: it was supposed to be here Monday
it should have come by now
say: I'm sorry it's late, let me find out why.

when: Caller received the wrong, damaged, or missing item.
examples: something was missing from my order
say: I'm sorry about that, let me look at your order.

when: Caller wants to place a new order.
examples: I want to buy two of those
I'd like to get the large one
say: Great, let me help you place that order.

when: Caller wants to change delivery address, time, or instructions.
examples: can you deliver to a different address
I want to reschedule the delivery
I need to change where it ships
say: Let me see if the delivery can still be changed.

when: Caller says a package is lost or marked delivered but not received.
examples: it says delivered but I don't have it
the tracking hasn't updated in days
say: I'm sorry, let me look into where it went.

when: Caller wants to schedule a new appointment.
examples: I'd like to book an appointment
I need to set up a time to come in
say: Sure, let me check availability.

when: Caller wants to move an existing appointment.
examples: I can't make it Tuesday, can we do another day
push it back a week please
say: Okay, let me look at your appointment.

when: Caller wants to cancel an appointment.
examples: I need to cancel my appointment
I won't be able to come in
please take me off the schedule
say: No problem, let me find that appointment.

when: Caller asks when their appointment is.
examples: do I have something this week
remind me what day I'm booked
say: Let me check when you're scheduled.

when: Caller asks about available dates or hours.
examples: what times do you have on Friday
what's the earliest I can come in
say: Let me see what times are open.

when: Caller picks or proposes a specific date or time slot.
examples: I'll take the three o'clock one
say: Great, let me see if that works.

when: Caller asks what to bring or how to prepare for an appointment.
examples: what do I need to bring
do I need to arrive early
is there anything I should do beforehand
say: Let me find the details for you.

when: Caller asks the price of a product or service.
examples: what do you charge for that
how much is the basic plan
say: Let me get the pricing for you.

when: Caller asks about business hours or locations.
say: Let me pull up that information.

when: Caller asks to compare options or what is included.
examples: what's the difference between the two plans
which plan is best for me
say: Good question, let me compare those for you.

when: Caller asks about discounts, promotions, or deals.
examples: is there a discount for me
can I get a better rate
say: Let me see what offers are available.

when: Caller asks about a policy such as returns, warranty, or fees.
examples: do you charge a late fee
how long do I have to cancel
say: Let me check the policy on that.

when: Caller asks whether a product or service is available or in stock.
examples: do you have that in stock
is that available in my area
say: Let me check on that availability.

when: Caller asks an open-ended informational question needing a lookup.
examples: I have a question about how this works
can you tell me about your services
I'm trying to find out some information
say: Sure, let me find that out for you.

when: Caller says a clear yes or agrees.
say: Great, got it.

when: Caller says a clear no or declines.
say: No problem, I understand.

when: Caller confirms that details read back are correct.
say: Thank you, I've noted that.

when: Caller authorizes the assistant to proceed with an action.
say: Okay, I'm taking care of that now.

when: Caller is unsure or hesitates.
say: No rush, take your time.

when: Caller reverses or stops an action they just agreed to.
say: Okay, I'll hold off on that.

when: Caller gives a short acknowledgement without a clear yes or no.
say: Okay, one moment.

when: Caller asks the assistant to wait while they find something.
examples: just a sec, let me grab it
wait one minute, I need to find my card
say: Sure, take your time.

when: Caller asks whether the assistant is still working or still on the line.
examples: hello, you still working on it
is it taking this long normally
say: Still here, just working on it.

when: Caller asks how long something will take.
examples: is this going to take long
when will you have an answer
say: Just a few more moments.

when: Caller says it is a bad time and asks to call back or pause.
examples: I'm in the middle of something
I'll have to call you back
say: No problem, we can pick this up whenever.

when: Caller says they are fetching a document, card, or number.
examples: let me find my account number
I'm going to get my card
hang on, looking for the paperwork
say: Take your time, I'll be right here.

when: Caller waits expectantly after asking something complex and says nothing more.
say: Thanks for waiting, I'm checking now.

when: Caller input is garbled, noisy, or mostly background sound.
say: Sorry, I'm having trouble hearing you.

when: Caller starts a sentence and trails off or is cut off.
say: Go ahead, I'm listening.

when: Caller says only fillers like um or hmm while thinking.
say: Take your time.

when: Caller says something unrelated to anything the assistant can help with.
examples: can you tell me a joke
who won the game last night
say: Ha, let me think about how I can best help.

when: Caller states several different needs at once.
examples: I need to pay my bill and also change my address and ask about a refund
two things, my balance and my appointment
I've got a couple of issues
say: Okay, let's take them one at a time.

when: Input appears to be the caller talking to someone else in the room.
examples: no honey I'm on the phone
just a minute, I'll be right there
say: No worries, I'll be here when you're ready.
